title: Consumer-side fanout optimizer and jitter smoothing for realtime console metrics
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and implement a consumer-side fanout optimizer for the realtime console metrics pipeline that reduces end-to-end jitter for downstream dashboards and alerting consumers. The goal is to smooth bursty ingress patterns without increasing tail latency, enforce fairness across tenants during spikes, and provide an operational knobset for trade-offs between immediacy and batching efficiency.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end 99th-percentile tail for console dashboards decreases by at least 20% under synthetic burst tests compared to current baseline
No increase in average end-to-end latency by more than 10% during steady-state traffic
Per-tenant throughput fairness ensured: when a noisy tenant spikes, other tenants retain at least 70% of pre-spike throughput (configurable policy)
Graceful fallback to existing ingress backpressure if local consumer buffer cannot keep up
Operational metrics emitted: consumer_buffer_occupancy, fanout_delay_ms_p95, tenant_throttle_ratio, jitter_smoothed_ms
Feature can be toggled per-environment and rolled out via console rollout with canary
updates: 2026-03-02 - Created ticket (Ava Martinez): initial problem statement after first-week incident where a single tenant blast caused dashboards to spike and rendered some alerting noisy.

2026-03-04 - Architecture sync (Liam O'Connor, Priya Rao, Marco Diaz): decided on a consumer-side approach (local slab buffer + adaptive release) vs upstream shaper. Rationale: lower coordination and faster rollout to Dedicated/Private customers.

2026-03-05 - Prototype spike test (Marco Diaz): local slab with time-windowed release reduced observed jitter by ~18% in lab (tail improved but noticed small average latency bump). Saved prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1287

2026-03-06 - Trade-off discussion (PM review - Jonah Singh): agreed to expose two operational knobs: release_window_ms (for jitter smoothing) and tenant_throttle_mode (drop|queue|prioritize). PM asked to default to queue with conservative time window.

2026-03-08 - Load test (QA - Anna Chen): ran multi-tenant 100k tps ingress with 10% noisy tenant blasts. Results: p99 reduced 22%, avg latency increased 6% under default config. Added test artifacts to docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Telemetry/Consumer+Fanout+Load+Tests

2026-03-09 - Review feedback (Infra - Nikhil Patel): noted potential memory pressure on small VMs for on-prem; action: implement soft-lease eviction and per-tenant memory caps. Added dependency ENG-271992 for per-tenant reservoir limits.

2026-03-11 - Security review checklist added (Ava Martinez): KMS access not required; no new external endpoints. Marked security_review_required = false. Will document audit logging for throttling decisions.

2026-03-12 - Implementation progress (Liam O'Connor): core release/emit loop implemented; unit tests cover adaptive-release heuristics. Preparing integration PR and dashboard panels. Next: run canary in staging and collect 48h traces.
notes: Implementation approach: lightweight per-consumer slab buffer that groups events into micro-batches bounded by a release_window and max_batch_tokens. An adaptive controller observes downstream ACKs and expands/contracts the release_window to target a configured downstream latency SLO. For multi-tenant fairness, maintain per-tenant credit counters and a weighted round-robin release; when memory pressure is detected, oldest low-priority tenant batches are soft-evicted (logged and counted). Operational concerns: must instrument detailed telemetry for the controller to avoid oscillation; include a mode that samples 1% of messages for trace IDs to validate ordering semantics post-eviction.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype in telemetry consumer side (done) - basic slab + release loop
Week 2: Add adaptive controller and per-tenant credits, implement soft-eviction and memory caps
Week 3: Add metrics dashboards, unit + integration tests, run staging canary
Week 4: Observability review, docs + runbook, rollout to production via console canary
